carrboro-town.label: Carrboro town drop-off locations and access

prep.label: Access
prep.text: Sign up through the partner link on the city’s page and choose a listed drop-off.

prep.label: Scope
prep.text: These are food-scrap carts. Use the city’s separate yard-waste route for grass, branches and leaves.

prep.label: Access
prep.text: The city limits these drop-off locations to Madison residents and taxpayers. Check site hours and what proof to bring.

prep.label: Which bin
prep.text: Use the orange food-scrap carts at Streets Division drop-off sites. The page describes farmers’ markets and county kiosks separately.

prep.label: Access
prep.text: The city currently describes this program for approved residents of multifamily housing. An application by itself does not unlock a bin.

prep.label: Unlocking
prep.text: Wait for approval and app instructions. The city describes requesting a separate unlocking method if you cannot use a smartphone.

prep.label: Access
prep.text: Choose a site and follow the city’s sign-up and welcome instructions to use the locked cart.

prep.label: Bag
prep.text: The drop-off instructions discuss both paper and compostable plastic. Use the linked materials guide to check the BPI mark.

prep.label: Access
prep.text: The city describes free residential drop-off for city residents and city employees. Register in CompostHere to unlock the container.

prep.label: Amount
prep.text: The city limits use to two gallons per person per 24-hour or weekend period and excludes commercial and event scraps.

prep.label: Location
prep.text: The town lists roll-out carts behind Town Hall. The market also posts that its compost drop-off moved there. Check the town’s current directions.

prep.label: Access
prep.text: The town lists an app requirement for the separate BigBelly bins at Jones Ferry and MLK Park. Check the type of bin at the site you plan to use.

tasks.label: Brown paper bag left in the bin

rules.text: The city excludes raw meat.
Cooked meat and animal or fish bones are on the city’s accepted list.
The city lists brown paper bags among accepted items.
The city excludes plastic and biodegradable products. The accepted list identifies brown paper bags as its collection option.
The city excludes tea bags and accepts loose tea leaves.
All meat and bones are excluded.
The food-scrap carts exclude cooked meat and bones.
The city says to empty the contents into the cart and keep paper bags out.
The city explicitly excludes compostable plastic bags.
The site accepts loose tea and excludes tea bags.
The bin program says all food scraps and lists meat, bones and seafood. Its drop-off list gives no separate raw-meat instruction. Ask the city if you need to confirm this exact case.
The city includes meat and bones in the bin program.
The drop-off announcement allows loose scraps or scraps in brown paper bags.
The city’s drop-off announcement describes loose scraps and brown paper bags. Confirm any certified plastic liner for this route.
The bin list identifies loose tea and excludes tea bags.
The materials list includes meat, fish and bones generally. Confirm raw meat if you are unsure about a particular item.
The city lists meat, fish and bones among accepted organics.
The drop-off instructions allow compostable paper bags.
The city accepts compostable plastic bags with the BPI mark. Check the linked list for its marking requirements.
The accepted-organics illustration includes a tea bag. The text list gives no bag-material instructions. Ask about your type before dropping it off.
The drop-off list includes meat generally. The city gives different rules for home composting, so confirm this specific case with staff.
The drop-off list includes residential meat scraps.
The city excludes plastic generally. Its HTML list does not discuss this exact certification. Follow the specific bin directions before using a liner.
The county lists meat and fish products. Call the county for confirmation if you need a specific raw-meat rule.
The county includes meat and small chicken and fish bones in its accepted list.
The county lists soiled paper food packaging that is entirely paper. Ask about the specific bag before dropping it off.
The county excludes compostable plastic bags even when BPI-certified.
The county includes tea bags and asks users to remove staples.
